title: DeleteWorkspaceFlow
wrapsNative: sheet(isPresented:content:) with interactiveDismissDisabled, holding a NavigationStack with navigationDestination(for:) for the steps; MonarchConsequenceList, MonarchButton, MonarchTypeToConfirmInput, MonarchInlineNotice, a nested sheet with MonarchStepUpAuthDialog, and MonarchEmptyState for the done screen
summary: A recipe, not a component: an owner deletes a workspace in a sheet that shows what will be deleted, offers an export and a transfer instead, asks for the workspace name, confirms it is them with MonarchStepUpAuthDialog, and ends on a done screen.
whenToUse: In workspace settings, behind a danger Delete workspace button that only owners see.
whenNotToUse: To leave a workspace use the leave workspace recipe. To remove a member use the revoke access recipe. To erase one person's data use the GDPR erase recipe.
api: MonarchButton("Delete workspace", systemImage: "trash", variant: .danger) { isOpen = true }

impact: MonarchConsequenceList([MonarchConsequence(.removed, "apps", count: 4), …], heading: "What will be deleted"); MonarchButton("Export data"); MonarchButton("Transfer ownership instead", variant: .ghost); NavigationLink("Continue", value: …)

confirm: MonarchTypeToConfirmInput(phrase: workspaceName, text: $typed, onMatchChange: { isMatched = $0 }); MonarchButton("Delete workspace", variant: .danger, isLoading: isDeleting).disabled(!isMatched)
.sheet(isPresented: $isVerifying) { MonarchStepUpAuthDialog(description:, onVerified: { delete() }, onVerify: { credential in … }) }
done: MonarchEmptyState("Workspace deleted", message:, kind: .success, actionTitle: "Close", action:)

states.name: impact
states.description: The first screen: a sentence, MonarchConsequenceList with the counts (apps, members, records, subscriptions, domains), an optional Keep a copy section with Export data, an optional Transfer it instead section, and Continue.

states.name: impact loading
states.description: Pass isLoading to MonarchConsequenceList and disable Continue with a caption saying to wait for the summary.

states.name: confirm
states.description: The pushed screen: "This cannot be undone." (or the scheduled date with a grace period), the type-to-confirm field, and a danger Delete workspace button disabled until the name matches.

states.name: verifying
states.description: MonarchStepUpAuthDialog in a nested sheet; the delete runs only after it succeeds.

states.name: deleting
states.description: The danger button shows its spinner and the sheet cannot be swiped away.

states.name: failed
states.description: A danger MonarchInlineNotice on the confirm screen, announced; the person can try again.

states.name: done
states.description: A success MonarchEmptyState, "Workspace deleted" or "Deletion scheduled", with Close; the app then navigates away.

appearance: Every part is an existing Monarch component or a system sheet and navigation bar in the theme: MonarchConsequenceList with its kind icons, MonarchSectionHeader for the optional sections, primary, secondary, ghost and danger MonarchButtons.
platformNotes: The web's DeleteWorkspaceFlow is one component built on a WizardDialog with numbered steps. On iOS it is a recipe: a sheet with a NavigationStack, so each step is a pushed screen with the system back button, which is how multi-step tasks work on a phone, and the step-up check is MonarchStepUpAuthDialog in a nested sheet. The web's impact counts become MonarchConsequence items with counts; its messages are written in the app. The web's gracePeriodDays changes only the copy ("Schedule deletion", the date) and is the app's choice here. Android composes the same recipe.
accessibility: The navigation title of each step is read when the step appears; the system back button returns to the previous step.
MonarchConsequenceList reads each line with its kind and count, so removed and changed do not depend on the icons.
MonarchTypeToConfirmInput announces when the typed name matches.
The disabled Delete workspace button has a caption that says why.
Failures are shown in words in a notice and announced; the sheet cannot be dismissed while deleting.
MonarchStepUpAuthDialog shows errors in words and supports the password, a code and the device owner check.
edgeCases: Check on the server that the person is an owner and re-authenticated; the recipe only gathers the confirmation.
Offer Transfer ownership instead only when there is another member who could own the workspace.
After the done screen closes, navigate away from the deleted workspace.
With a grace period, say when the deletion happens and how to cancel it.
